sprint_a.note: Subject 102 (basketball), 'RunningNoBall': the fastest steady straight run found in the library, 5.04 m/s on the reference man, a long driving stride (3.19 m), the heels kicked high, the trunk 30 degrees forward as he ran it. Driven to 5.8: the loop played in 17 frames for the capture's 19, the feet's fore-and-aft reach about the hips 3 per cent longer (by IK), the feet locked again; a foot coming in to land keeps its heel 4.5 cm up (it lands on the ball).
sprint_a.pace_how: the ground speeds the clip can be played at (the game plays it at speed / (stride / length), the planted feet then going back at the ground's speed at any of them, so what limits it is time): no slower than 0.80 and no faster than 1.30 of the capture's own time (slowed film floats, hurried film jerks: a clip already played faster than captured has less room above), no slower than 0.85 of the clip's own time for a gait with both feet in the air (it stops reading as that gait), and the steps a second inside a man's range for the gait (sprint and dash 3.0 to 4.7, jog 2.1 to 3.3, walk 1.0 to 2.7); a walk, with a foot always down, may be played from 0.565 to 1.33 of its time. Set from these measures and the stills on the reference man; not watched as moving film. On a soldier file the planted foot's slide decides as well.

limp_l.note: Subject 142 (stylized walks), 'Painfulleftknee': a real limp, the LEFT leg the hurt one as captured (no mirror): the left knee held stiff (bent 21 degrees in its stance, the right 42), the left foot a shorter time on the ground, the trunk forward and dipping onto it. His faster pass (1.05 m/s). He gets off the hurt leg sooner than he did: the loop's time runs 24 per cent faster in the middle of its stance and slower on the good leg (favour), so the left foot is down 13 frames against the right's 19 (15 against 17 as captured); the right toe's snap at its toe-off eased (330 deg/s), the knees kept within 10 degrees of their hinge. Mended again 26 November after the picture review (from the game's camera it read as a slow walk): favour 0.40, so the left foot is down 12 frames against the right's 20; the trunk lurching 10 degrees over the hurt leg while it bears him (the pelvis 3 cm over it, the head dipping 8 degrees); the hurt leg swung through stiff (the knee kept under 20 degrees of bend), the pelvis hitched 6 degrees on that side and the leg swung out 8 degrees round, not through.

stumble.note: No trip inside a run in the library (104_13 'StumbleWalk' is a walk; 16_08 and 16_57 are stops), so it is keyed on run_a (CMU 35_18, the file's own run): the first frame is run_a's first, the last run_a's frame 16 (0.5333 s). _about.credit: The data used in this project was obtained from mocap.cs.cmu.edu. The database was created with funding from NSF EIA-0196217.
_about.rig: human.py (27 bones), reference man human.build(seed=0, stand=0.02, curl=(30, 45, 25)), 1.75 m
_about.frame: Blender's: x forward, y LEFT, z up, metres. For Unreal's y-right frame mirror quaternions as (w, -x, y, -z) and locations as (x, -y, z).
_about.bones: per bone, per frame, [w, x, y, z]: the rotation D relative to the bone's rest, in its PARENT's space (the bone's local rotation in its parent's frame = D * RestLocal). Blender pose quaternion = RestLocal^-1 * D * RestLocal.
_about.pelvis_loc: per frame [x, y, z]: the pelvis head's offset from its rest place, in the armature's space. The root bone never moves (IN PLACE). Scale it by (this man's leg / leg) for another man.
_about.loops: frames includes the closing frame, equal to the first: length = (frames - 1) / fps. Play rate for a travel loop = speed / stride * length (stride: metres travelled per loop by this 1.75 m man).
_about.made: gaits_mocap.py: CMU takes cut as mocap.py cuts its own, the gaits' postures laid over them (each clip's note and build.laid_over)
_about.keying: build.stance: the frames each foot was held on the ground by the foot lock, [first, one past the last], counted on past the seam for a step that crosses it (the stumble's: on its own frames; its left [7, 10] is the caught toe held, not a step). A sprint's or a dash's foot is down 3 to 5 frames (0.10 to 0.17 s): planted on keys at 15 a second a step is left one key, and run_styles.py's plant refused the three sprints and dash_b on a soldier file (soldier_USA, in memory); so gaits.py plants those on keys at 30 a second and then keeps every other key, 15 a second as every clip the game has, the loop begun where the kept keys leave the soles least under the ground between them (a key near the middle of each stance; key_phase). On the reference man a moving foot is kept 4 cm clear of its lowest, so a ball within 3.5 cm of its lowest is a planted one. The stumble is not a loop: run_styles.make_clip closes every clip as one, so it needs its own keying (first key run_a's frame 0, last key run_a's frame at `rejoin`).

_rest.about: the reference man's rest (mocap_cmu/rest_ref.json): bone order (parents first), parent names, rest turns (Blender's axes)

_reference.about: run_styles_clips.json's run_a and advance_a (the file's own run and advance) measured the same way, to set the gaits against
